listing_note: Euronext Amsterdam ordinary listing. Model is built per ORDINARY SHARE in EUR (31.5m diluted ordinary shares FY2025), consistent with Adyen's reporting currency and share structure. The US OTC ADR (ADYEY) trades 1 ADR = 1/100th of one ordinary share: IV_per_ADR_USD = IV_per_ordinary_EUR x EURUSD / 100. Cross-check: ADYEY last traded $10.70; EUR930.30 x 1.1562 / 100 = $10.756, matching within normal bid/ask and timing noise.

notes.net_cash_derivation: Gross balance-sheet cash of EUR 10,797.4m (FY2025) is overwhelmingly merchant settlement float held in transit as a licensed payment institution/bank and is NOT available to equity holders. Own-cash = Cash (10,797.4) - Payables to merchants (6,371.8) + Receivables from merchants/FI (562.0) = EUR 4,987.6m. Net cash = Own-cash - Lease liabilities (252.4) = EUR 4,734.8m (rounded 4,735.2 in calc). This is used as the negative net_debt in the DCF bridge. NEVER use the raw EUR10.8bn balance-sheet cash figure -- it would overstate IV by roughly EUR190/share of money that belongs to merchants, not shareholders.
notes.interest_income_treatment: Adyen's income statement has TWO distinct interest/finance lines that must not be confused. (1) 'Net interest income' (FY2025 EUR12.573m) is interest earned on embedded-finance products (Accounts, Capital loans/advances) net of interest paid on deposited Accounts funds -- this is a genuine, recurring OPERATING revenue stream and is already included inside 'Net revenue' (NetRevenue in the CSV); it is NOT stripped. (2) 'Finance income' (FY2025 EUR267.550m gross, EUR260.786m cash-received) is interest earned on Adyen's OWN cash/investment balances (including the float) and sits below the operating line in 'Net finance income' -- this is what inflates reported FCF via the float/own-cash pile that is separately added back to enterprise value in the net-cash bridge. To avoid double-counting the cash pile (once via net cash in the EV bridge, once via the interest it earns inside FCF), Finance income is STRIPPED from reported FCF to compute owner FCF. This is fully consistent: float-related operating interest stays in revenue/FCF (it recurs with transaction volume), only interest on Adyen's own invested cash balance is removed. Verified against ADYEN.AS_Annual_FY2025.txt: note 10 (Finance income, line 7101), accounting policy statement (line 7499), and the explicit clarification at line 7518 that interest on cash balances outside the embedded-finance products is NOT classified within net interest income.
notes.fcf_definition: Reported FCF = EBITDA - CapEx (company convention; Adyen does not report unlevered FCF directly). Owner FCF (historical, FY2020-2025 actuals) = Reported FCF - SBC - Finance income (own-cash interest). Applied consistently across FY2020-FY2025 so the historical CAGRs in historical_growth are computed on a like-for-like owner-FCF series. For the FORWARD projections (Step 1c component build), SBC is charged exactly once via EBIT (adj_EBITDA - SBC - D&A) and Finance income is never in EBITDA/EBIT to begin with (it is a below-the-line finance item, not an operating line) -- see notes.sbc_charged_once_warning.
notes.sbc_charged_once_warning: IMPORTANT FOR FUTURE EDITS: in the forward component build, SBC is subtracted exactly ONCE, inside EBIT = adj_EBITDA - SBC - D&A. NOPAT = EBIT x (1 - cash_tax_rate) already reflects the SBC charge (tax-effected). owner_fcf = NOPAT + D&A - Capex - Working Capital. Do NOT subtract SBC again anywhere downstream of NOPAT -- that would double-charge it and understate FCF, and do NOT add SBC back after NOPAT either -- that would net the whole adjustment to roughly zero and defeat the purpose of Step 1b/1c. A prior version of this model computed owner_fcf as nopat + d_and_a - capex + working_capital (working capital ADDED rather than subtracted); this was corrected 2026-08-09 to nopat + d_and_a - capex - working_capital because Adyen's FY2025 cash flow statement (line 7293/7300) shows working capital is a net USE of cash as revenue grows (receivables from merchants/FI increase faster than payables to merchants), not a source -- confirmed net WC cash effect FY2025 = -EUR53.9m (receivables -EUR85.0m, payables +EUR31.1m). The earlier '+working_capital' sign was the actual bug, not a double-SBC-charge (EBIT/NOPAT were and remain correct: SBC is charged exactly once, via EBIT, and is never added back).
notes.fcf_no_sbc_memo: Memo: value per share if SBC were treated as a fully non-cash expense (i.e., EBIT computed WITHOUT subtracting SBC, tax-effected consistently, everything else held constant) is EUR767.16/share in the base case vs the headline EUR749.38/share actually used -- a EUR17.79/share spread (post-tax present value of ~EUR38-47m/yr of pre-tax SBC across the 5-year explicit horizon plus its effect on the terminal value). This spread is the honest, quantified cost of ignoring Adyen's stock-based compensation; because Adyen conducts zero buybacks, the same cost also shows up as uncovered share dilution (~0.65%/yr) in the terminal share count used to divide equity value.
notes.growth_deceleration_context: FY2026 guidance is 20-22% CC net revenue growth, but Q1-2026 printed +16% reported / +20% CC with Digital (56% of revenue) decelerating to +9% reported/+13% CC -- the slowest pillar print in company history. EUR weakness vs USD has also been a reported-growth headwind (FY2025 net revenue +18% reported vs +21% CC). Management pushed the 55%+ EBITDA margin target from 2026 to 2028, and in June 2026 revised pricing for large/high-volume merchants, pressuring take rate. Base case therefore anchors Y1 reported growth near 18% (below the 20-22% CC guide, reflecting FX drag and pricing-mix headwinds) and decelerates toward terminal, rather than extrapolating the historical 21% 3yr net-revenue CAGR flat.
notes.horizon_rationale: 5-year explicit horizon used: the component-built owner-FCF margin is already fairly mature by Year 5 in the base case (34.8% Y1 -> 36.8% Y5, a modest ~2pp drift versus a >4pp gap that would indicate an immature terminal year), so a 10-year build is not required to avoid understating the business the way it was for hypergrowth/subscription names.

inputs.interest_income_note: 'Finance income' line (own-cash/float interest), NOT the 'Net interest income' embedded-finance product line which stays inside NetRevenue -- see notes.interest_income_treatment
inputs.sbc_source: ADYEN.AS_Annual_FY2025.txt cash flow statement adjustments (SBC EUR43.457m) and Consolidated Statement of Comprehensive Income (Finance income EUR267,550 thousand = EUR267.550m), both in EUR thousands in the filing, converted to millions
inputs.buyback_note: Adyen conducts zero share buybacks and pays zero dividends -- 100% earnings retention. This is explicit in the Analysis JSON business_model description.
inputs.annual_share_growth_note: Derived from observed share count growth 30.5m (FY2020) -> 31.5m (FY2025), a 5-year CAGR of 0.647%/yr, used directly as the projected dilution rate since buybacks are zero and 100% of SBC is uncovered.

historical_growth.revenue_basis: NetRevenue column (net revenue is Adyen's reported top line; the CSV Revenue column is intentionally blank)
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr (net revenue), used as the historical anchor but NOT extrapolated flat -- Year-1 base case growth is set below this (18%) to reflect the FY2026 guidance context, Q1-2026 deceleration, FX headwind and June-2026 pricing revision documented in notes.growth_deceleration_context
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Shareholders'-equity CAGR (~30% 3yr / ~34% 5yr) is materially higher than net-revenue CAGR (~21% 3yr / ~28% 5yr). This divergence is an artifact of 100% earnings retention (Adyen pays no dividends and conducts no buybacks), not superior underlying unit economics -- do not use equity CAGR as the growth anchor for a company with a purely additive retention effect.
historical_growth.notes: The SBC-adjusted (owner) FCF CAGR (10.7% 3yr / 18.1% 5yr) is MATERIALLY BELOW the reported FCF CAGR (21.2% 3yr / 25.6% 5yr). This gap is driven mostly by the 'Finance income' strip (own-cash interest income spiked from EUR29.3m in FY2022 to EUR246-350m in FY2023-2025 as rates rose, a rate-cycle windfall, not operating performance) rather than by SBC alone (SBC is genuinely small for Adyen, ~1.8% of FY2025 net revenue). Reported FCF growth therefore significantly overstates the growth of Adyen's core operating cash generation; owner FCF is the correct base for the DCF. (This historical series uses actual reported working-capital movements embedded in reported_fcf, not the forward wc_capture proxy used in projections.)

base.growth_rate_basis: Net revenue growth, reported (not CC). Starts below the 20-22% CC FY2026 guidance to reflect FX headwind, Q1-2026 Digital-pillar deceleration (+9% reported) and the June-2026 large-merchant pricing revision, then decelerates toward terminal.
base.wc_capture_note: Working capital modeled as wc_capture x (YoY change in Net Revenue), SUBTRACTED as a net use of cash. Adyen's FY2025 cash flow statement shows growth drives a net working-capital cash OUTFLOW (receivables from merchants/FI grow faster than payables to merchants: -EUR85.0m vs +EUR31.1m, net -EUR53.9m), so a growing net revenue base consumes cash on this line, unlike a SaaS deferred-revenue business where growth would be a source of cash. Capture rate set conservatively at 5% of the revenue increase.
base.cash_tax_note: FY2025 effective cash tax rate was 23.8%; ramped gradually to the Dutch statutory rate of 25.8% by Year 5.

bull.growth_rate_basis: Growth holds near/above FY2026 guidance midpoint: Platforms (+50% FY2025) continues to inflect, Digital pillar reaccelerates, North America execution improves, Talon.One/Orb cross-sell contributes, EBITDA margin pulls the 55%+ target forward.

bear.growth_rate_basis: Stripe/Checkout.com competitive pressure intensifies, June-2026 pricing revision proves the start of sustained take-rate compression, Digital pillar deceleration persists, leadership-transition disruption (CFO departure, Co-CEO health step-back, first-ever M&A integration) weighs on execution, margin expansion stalls below the 2028 target.

base.working_capital_note: Net use of cash (SUBTRACTED in owner_fcf), not a source -- see assumptions.base.wc_capture_note
base.owner_fcf_formula: nopat + d_and_a - capex - working_capital (SBC charged exactly once via EBIT, never added back -- see notes.sbc_charged_once_warning)

bull.working_capital_note: Net use of cash (SUBTRACTED in owner_fcf), not a source

bear.working_capital_note: Net use of cash (SUBTRACTED in owner_fcf), not a source

current_ev_fcf_multiple_check.note: Current market EV/owner-FCF (~31.9x, unaffected by the working-capital fix since it is computed on FY2025 actuals) is well ABOVE every scenario's implied exit multiple (base 14.2x, bull 18.0x, bear 11.1x) -- the model assumes continued de-rating toward more normal payments-platform multiples, NOT multiple expansion. This is consistent with Adyen's continuous de-rating since IPO (see sanity_check).

entry_price.note: Entry price uses base-case owner FCF path (interim years discounted at 15%) plus the base-case Gordon terminal value (still computed at WACC=10%, the fair exit price) discounted back to today at 15%, plus net cash, divided by the Year-5 projected share count. Sits below intrinsic value (EUR749.38) as expected since base-case growth (~14% average) is below the 15% hurdle.

sensitivity.note: Intrinsic value per ordinary share (EUR), base-case owner-FCF path (growth 18/16/14/12/10%, EBITDA margin ramp 53.5%->56.5%, working capital subtracted as a net use of cash). Cap of 20x terminal FCF binds at the low-WACC/high-terminal-growth corner (WACC=8%, terminal growth 3.25% and 3.75% both hit the EUR1,005.90 cap).

wacc_rationale: Base-case WACC of 10.0% reflects: (1) Adyen is a large-cap (~EUR29bn market cap FY2025-end context, now ~EUR29.3bn at current price), highly profitable, carries no financial debt (only IFRS-16 lease liabilities) and generates strong owner FCF margins (~33-37%) -- these attributes argue for a WACC toward the lower end of the 9.5-11% range typically defensible for a company this size and quality; (2) offsetting that, genuine and rising execution/competition risk (Stripe processing $1.9tn vs Adyen's EUR1.4tn in 2025, +34% vs +8% reported TPV growth), a documented pricing-power challenge (June 2026 large-merchant pricing revision), an unusually concentrated leadership transition (Co-CEO health step-back, CFO departure, new CPO, first-ever M&A integration all within months), and a continuous multi-year de-rating trend argue against using the lowest end of the range. 10.0% (bull 9.0%, bear 11.5%) is used as a defensible mid-point that is meaningfully above a mega-cap-compounder WACC (e.g., ~8-9% typical for AAPL/V) but below a small/distressed-company WACC, reflecting Adyen's size/quality offset by real, currently-crystallizing risk.

implied_multiples.pe_note: P/E not computed directly (net income includes the Finance-income line stripped from owner FCF); use EV/owner-FCF and P/S as the primary cross-checks instead.
implied_multiples.pb_note: Base-case implied equity value (EUR24,379.3m) / FY2025 shareholders' equity (EUR5,285.4m) = 4.61x. Current market P/B for context: current price EUR930.30 x 31.5m shares / EUR5,285.4m equity = 5.55x.
implied_multiples.ev_owner_fcf_note: Base-case implied exit multiple (TV_5/FCF_5) of 14.2x -- see valuation.base.implied_exit_multiple
implied_multiples.p_sales_note: Base-case equity value (EUR24,379.3m) / FY2025 net revenue (EUR2,364.2m) = 10.3x on TODAY's revenue base; on Year-5 projected revenue (EUR4,545.1m) it is 5.4x -- both well below historical P/S multiples

historical_averages_ex_outliers.outliers_excluded: 2020-2021 (COVID-era hypergrowth bubble: FY-end trailing P/E 200.9x/116.2x, EV/EBITDA 130.3x/85.3x)

sanity_check.diagnosis: Adyen has DE-RATED CONTINUOUSLY since IPO across every multiple (FY-end trailing P/E 151x in 2018 -> a 2020 COVID-era bubble peak of 201x -> 37.2x at FY2025-end -> ~25x today at EUR930.30 against FY2025 EPS; EV/EBITDA 89.8x in 2019 -> 130.3x bubble peak -> 28.3x at FY2025-end). The corrected base-case DCF implies an EV/owner-FCF exit multiple of 14.2x, a P/B of 4.61x and a P/S of 5.4x on Year-5 revenue -- BELOW even the cheapest historical FY-end multiples in the company's public history (37.2x trailing P/E, 28.3x EV/EBITDA, 16.7x P/S, 7.5x P/B at FY2025-end). This is consistent with the current market price itself already sitting at a 25x-ish trailing multiple after a ~33-42% YTD-2026 drawdown (Feb-2026 guidance cut, May-2026 CFO resignation, June-2026 pricing revision/analyst downgrades) and ~72% below the August-2021 peak. Per the task's explicit guidance, the historical averages (ex-2020-2021 hypergrowth outliers: ~71x P/E, ~52x EV/EBITDA, ~33x P/S) are NOT treated as a re-rating target -- this check is ONE-DIRECTIONAL, guarding only against the model implying a valuation ABOVE what the market has historically paid even at its most generous (ex-bubble) multiples. Since every scenario's implied exit multiple sits below the cheapest ex-outlier historical print, and well below the current ~32x EV/owner-FCF the market is paying today, the DCF assumes continued de-rating (consistent with the multi-year trend) rather than re-rating, and the sanity check PASSES with no fix required. The working-capital sign correction (2026-08-09) LOWERED every scenario's IV, which if anything strengthens the pass (the model was already comfortably below the historical floor before the fix and remains so after it).
sanity_check.context: Current price EUR930.30 sits roughly mid-way through the 2026 de-rating (down from EUR1,570 FY2024-end and EUR1,253 FY2025-end closes). Corrected base-case DCF value of EUR749.38 (-19.4% downside) implies the market has NOT yet fully priced in the growth-deceleration/pricing-pressure risks the model bakes in via a below-guidance Year-1 growth rate, a genuinely-charged SBC expense, and a conservative 14.2x exit multiple; conversely the bull case (EUR1,069.17, +14.9%) requires guidance to hold and margin expansion to pull forward, which is plausible but not the central case given the June-2026 pricing revision and Q1-2026 Digital deceleration.

2026-08-09_wc_sign_fix.issue_as_reported: Owner FCF appeared to exceed a from-assumptions rebuild by ~EUR41-45m/yr in every scenario/year, diagnosed by the reporter as SBC being deducted (in EBIT) and then added back (post-NOPAT), netting the whole SBC adjustment to ~zero.
2026-08-09_wc_sign_fix.root_cause_confirmed: EBIT and NOPAT were and are correct (SBC charged exactly once, via EBIT = adj_EBITDA - SBC - D&A; never added back anywhere). The actual bug was a WORKING CAPITAL SIGN ERROR: owner_fcf was computed as nopat + d_and_a - capex + working_capital (treating a growing net-revenue-driven working-capital balance as a SOURCE of cash), when Adyen's FY2025 cash flow statement shows it is a NET USE of cash as revenue grows (receivables from merchants/FI increase faster than payables to merchants: -EUR85.0m vs +EUR31.1m, net -EUR53.9m). Corrected formula: owner_fcf = nopat + d_and_a - capex - working_capital.
2026-08-09_wc_sign_fix.magnitude: Base-case owner_fcf reduced by ~EUR35-45m/yr (2x the working_capital line, since the sign flip both removes the erroneous addition and applies the correct subtraction), reducing base IV from EUR765.64 to EUR749.38 (-2.1%), bull IV from EUR1,106.35 to EUR1,069.17 (-3.4%), bear IV from EUR516.31 to EUR510.16 (-1.2%). Entry price reduced from EUR653.50 to EUR640.05. Weighted IV reduced from EUR788.49 to EUR769.52.
